Criteria text

Agent verification criteria — version 4

Scope: TASK.md's one already-held plug, either white-like or black-like. The goal is blades upward and a steady airborne hold. Pickup, transport and placement in the full demonstration are excluded. These are my own simulation criteria, not official success criteria.

Evidence and reconstruction uncertainty

Turn intervals measured in the final reconstruction (version 2) are: white frames 100–140 (3.333–4.667 s), black 310–340 (10.333–11.333 s). Visible evidence: thumb on the near housing face, index curling/repositioning on the opposite/top side, middle assisting; blades move from roughly horizontal to upward. Pixel blade-hole centre annotations constrain white orientation. Hidden surfaces and exact contacts are inferred. Whole-object metric geometry is approximate; mass, inertia and friction are priors. Rotation estimates have substantial uncertainty under occlusion. The reference contract assigns combined endpoint rotation scales of12/35deg for clear/partial views. A sensitivity calculation with those scales and an assumed8deg wrist scale gives nominal5–95% ranges about43–110deg white and44–114deg black. These are sensitivity envelopes under assumed errors, not calibrated confidence intervals or ground-truth bounds. The visible blade-axis change, airborne handling and final goal are stronger evidence than the precise twist angle. Measured white broad relative rotation 70.7deg about object axis [.9548,-.2517,.1583], world rotation93.1deg, wrist23.8deg in1.333s. Its start overlaps pickup; the conservatively airborne f113–140 subset is47.8deg relative to wrist, so it does not define the primitive. Black f310–340 is a clearer already-airborne turn: relative72.3deg about object axis [.8370,.2060,.5069], world90.9deg, wrist33.1deg in1.0s. Palm angle from down averages21.7deg white /59.4deg black. The robot may choose the oblique palm-down white wrist pose and hold it approximately fixed; this shifts more rotation to its fingers. Time is allowed up to3s for the turn versus~1s human, a conservative control choice for a different hand. These deviations preserve finger-driven airborne handling.

Deployment envelope and limitations

Goal and skill conditions apply to any stable placement of either plug in the selected starting grasp. Finite simulation trials cannot establish the entire unbounded real deployment distribution. Training and verification will explicitly specify the chosen grasp, both mesh variants, position/orientation spread, mass/inertia/friction/size ranges, and an out-of-range stress distribution. Starts must be genuine free-body opposed grasps above the table; no support, weld, external object force or pose override operates during an episode. A stationary-finger baseline must retain the side-on plug without accomplishing the turn, excluding a preloaded passive flip.

Ordered stages (4 s episodes)

  1. retained: the first 0.25 s shows a hand-held opposed grasp, without contact with environment. Standard predicates: held_s >= 0.25 and opposed_s >= 0.25. Custom state-based checks also require an initial stable grasp and prohibit a drop throughout the episode.
  2. turned: a significant object rotation relative to wrist occurs during one opposed interval, with fingers visibly moving, and ends blades-up. Threshold for opposed_rel_rotation_deg is >=55 degrees, rounded upward from75% of the clearer black reference72.3deg (54.225deg). passive_rel_rotation_deg <=15 degrees: a deliberately strict bound relative to the reference's ~70-degree active turn and the hardware-independent 0.30 rad/s joint-motion indicator. final_axis_angle_deg with object_axis=[0,0,1], world_axis=[0,0,1] <=15 degrees. Fifteen degrees is a chosen physical upright tolerance, not a fitted measurement; the video ends with plugs standing with nearly vertical blades. goal_error_deg <=25 degrees with equivalent upright yaw goals; yaw is not part of TASK.md. wrist.max_rotation_deg <=15 degrees from start, so wrist rotation cannot explain most of the turn. Finger-specific excursion and the rendered rollout must support active thumb/opposing-finger manipulation, rather than motion confined to unrelated digits.
  3. steady: keep blades within 15 degrees of world up for the last uninterrupted 1 s, keep holding with no environmental contact, and keep maximum object linear speed <=0.02 m/s and angular speed <=0.20 rad/s over that second. These are physical steady-hold assumptions (2 cm and 11.5 degrees per second upper bounds), stricter than merely reaching an upright frame. Standard predicates include touching_hand_at_end>=1, touching_environment_at_end<=0, held_s>=3.9, environment_contact_s<=0, last_second_max_speed_m_s<=0.02, last_second_max_angular_speed_rad_s<=0.20, and final_axis_angle_deg<=15. Custom judge also checks continuous retention (no contact gap >0.04 s), height/reach, both thumb and a non-palm opposing digit, and ordered completion.

Every controller tick must obey hardware/SPECS.md: joint position within URDF limits ±0.02 rad, absolute speed within published limits, effort at or below saturation. No hardware-violation episode is a success. Demand saturation is reported separately.

Suite rates and evidence

Task and deployment skill pass rate: 0.80, with 0 hardware-violation episodes. This is an agent-chosen minimum reliability for a diverse but bounded manipulation skill; it does not imply universal robustness. Report rates and Wilson intervals, per-kind results, every stage funnel, failure videos and stress limitations. Use fixed dev seeds before checkpoint selection; a fresh final task gate of at least 128 episodes supplies the verdict. Primitive feasibility pass rate: 0.25 on documented narrow valid starts, sufficient to establish that the full contact-rich motion exists in the model. Skill mastery and library acceptance require >=0.80 with a deployable PPO-trained network, before whole-task training. A feasible script is only a baseline, not a learned result.

Numerical checks are necessary, not sufficient. Inspect successful and failed videos from three views, compare with the demonstration, and withhold a passing verdict if the mechanism visibly differs (wrist-only turning, supported pivot, passive slipping, or fingers passing through the plug). Verify no simulator state is overwritten to move the object, and report deepest contact penetration and model uncertainties.

The primitive reference is research/reference_motion.npz, object black, interval [310/30,340/30]; this names the black demonstration scene item, while each simulation episode calls its one plug object plug. All deployment configurations and domain ranges will be recorded before freezing the suites. Thresholds are chosen now before policy evaluation; changes require a new criteria version with a physical reason.

Revision2 clarifies uncertainty using the completed reference and sensitivity calculation. Goal, skill thresholds, stages and pass rates are unchanged; no policy has yet been evaluated.

Revision3 (before PPO and suite2): clarify a robot-specific initial grasp and stricter activity implementation. Use the measured black-turn wrist orientation [0.2649166,-0.1286708,-0.9484266,0.1172604], with bounded assistance as before. The physical initial grasp is retargeted kinematically to each sampled plug placement by thumb/index housing pad IK, then released to free-body holding under rate-limited hardware targets; there is no resampling of failed placements. The first0.25s must have >=96% opposed samples and hand-contact gaps may not exceed40ms. During the active turn, at least40deg of accumulated relative rotation must coincide with both thumb and an actually-contacting opposing digit moving at joint-speed norm>0.10rad/s; this is an additional physical activity assumption (~73% of the55deg turn threshold), not a measurement of the human. The last1s must have >=96% opposed samples. Goal, passive-turn, wrist,55deg turn, steady-speed, hardware and pass-rate thresholds remain unchanged. These clarifications tighten the custom checks and distinguish a genuine already-held pose from inserting an object into unchanged fingers. They do not relabel earlier gates.

Revision4: correct the coordinate expression of the unchanged world-upright goal. The evaluator previously compared the final object in the final wrist frame against an upright goal expressed in the INITIAL wrist frame. This mixed two frames when the wrist moved. For each episode, goal_rel_orientation is now R_hand_final^T R_world_upright_yaw, so angle(R_hand_final^T R_object_final, R_hand_final^T R_goal_world) equals the intended world-orientation error. The world goal, equivalent yaw set,25deg relative-goal threshold,15deg blade-up bound,55deg active turn,15deg wrist/passive bounds,steady thresholds and.80/zeroHW rates are unchanged. The goal frame conversion uses the final hand pose only to express the same fixed world goal, never to change that goal. Earlier suite versions and verdicts are not relabeled. The temporary operator-preload weld is reset-only and must be inactive in every episode state; any active fixture vetoes retained/turned/steady.

Starts must be genuine free-body opposed grasps above the table; no support, weld, external object force or pose override operates during an episode. A stationary-finger baseline must retain the side-on plug without accomplishing the turn, excluding a preloaded passive flip.

Ordered stages (4 s episodes)

  1. retained: the first 0.25 s shows a hand-held opposed grasp, without contact with environment. Standard predicates: held_s >= 0.25 and opposed_s >= 0.25. Custom state-based checks also require an initial stable grasp and prohibit a drop throughout the episode.
  2. turned: a significant object rotation relative to wrist occurs during one opposed interval, with fingers visibly moving, and ends blades-up. Threshold for opposed_rel_rotation_deg is >=55 degrees, rounded upward from75% of the clearer black reference72.3deg (54.225deg). passive_rel_rotation_deg <=15 degrees: a deliberately strict bound relative to the reference's ~70-degree active turn and the hardware-independent 0.30 rad/s joint-motion indicator. final_axis_angle_deg with object_axis=[0,0,1], world_axis=[0,0,1] <=15 degrees. Fifteen degrees is a chosen physical upright tolerance, not a fitted measurement; the video ends with plugs standing with nearly vertical blades. goal_error_deg <=25 degrees with equivalent upright yaw goals; yaw is not part of TASK.md. wrist.max_rotation_deg <=15 degrees from start, so wrist rotation cannot explain most of the turn. Finger-specific excursion and the rendered rollout must support active thumb/opposing-finger manipulation, rather than motion confined to unrelated digits.
  3. steady: keep blades within 15 degrees of world up for the last uninterrupted 1 s, keep holding with no environmental contact, and keep maximum object linear speed <=0.02 m/s and angular speed <=0.20 rad/s over that second. These are physical steady-hold assumptions (2 cm and 11.5 degrees per second upper bounds), stricter than merely reaching an upright frame. Standard predicates include touching_hand_at_end>=1, touching_environment_at_end<=0, held_s>=3.9, environment_contact_s<=0, last_second_max_speed_m_s<=0.02, last_second_max_angular_speed_rad_s<=0.20, and final_axis_angle_deg<=15. Custom judge also checks continuous retention (no contact gap >0.04 s), height/reach, both thumb and a non-palm opposing digit, and ordered completion.

Every controller tick must obey hardware/SPECS.md: joint position within URDF limits ±0.02 rad, absolute speed within published limits, effort at or below saturation. No hardware-violation episode is a success. Demand saturation is reported separately.

Suite rates and evidence

Task and deployment skill pass rate: 0.80, with 0 hardware-violation episodes. This is an agent-chosen minimum reliability for a diverse but bounded manipulation skill; it does not imply universal robustness. Report rates and Wilson intervals, per-kind results, every stage funnel, failure videos and stress limitations. Use fixed dev seeds before checkpoint selection; a fresh final task gate of at least 128 episodes supplies the verdict. Primitive feasibility pass rate: 0.25 on documented narrow valid starts, sufficient to establish that the full contact-rich motion exists in the model. Skill mastery and library acceptance require >=0.80 with a deployable PPO-trained network, before whole-task training. A feasible script is only a baseline, not a learned result.

Numerical checks are necessary, not sufficient. Inspect successful and failed videos from three views, compare with the demonstration, and withhold a passing verdict if the mechanism visibly differs (wrist-only turning, supported pivot, passive slipping, or fingers passing through the plug). Verify no simulator state is overwritten to move the object, and report deepest contact penetration and model uncertainties.

The primitive reference is research/reference_motion.npz, object black, interval [310/30,340/30]; this names the black demonstration scene item, while each simulation episode calls its one plug object plug. All deployment configurations and domain ranges will be recorded before freezing the suites. Thresholds are chosen now before policy evaluation; changes require a new criteria version with a physical reason.
